 Nxled seeks semis incentive vs Creamline
 By Niel Victor C. Masoy
 November 17, 2026
 50
 Resize 
 Small 
 Medium 
 Large 
 Read this in The Manila Times digital edition. 
 THE stakes are high when the Nxled Chameleons and the Creamline Cool Smashers collide in the PVL All-Filipino Conference Siklab Series at the PhilSports Arena on Tuesday.
 Game time is set at 6 p.m.
 Secured of a semifinal seat and still unbeaten at 6-0 with 17 points, the league-leading Nxled looks to clinch a twice-to-beat advantage this time around.
 That is easier said than done against the defending champ Creamline, which looks to grab one of the last two semis seats and snap its two-game skid including a 25-23, 13-25, 23-25, 25-22, 13-15 defeat to Choco Mucho last Thursday.
 The Cool Smashers dropped to 4-2 with 13 points in third place, but would secure a Final Four spot with a win against the Chameleons even if they lose their final eliminations match against the semis-bound and second seed Farm Fresh Foxies (5-2, 14 points) on Nov. 21.

 The fourth-running PLDT High Speed Hitters (4-3, 13 points) and the fifth seed Flying Titans (4-3, 12 points) will face each other at the end of eliminations, meaning one of them will incur a fourth loss and thus Creamline would be safe even with a 5-3 slate.
 Nxled head coach Ettore Guidetti said that preparation is the key for his team which wraps its elimination round campaign against Zus Coffee on Nov. 21.
 Advertisement 
 Nxled’s Brooke Van Sickle attacks against Akari’s Celine Domingo and Eli Soyud. PVL PHOTO
 "I really think that the only way to play at our best is to prepare all the games in the way that we have done in the last four or five months," the Italian coach said.
 "We know that we have a very big potential. And we know that we are going to play against two teams that they got an incredible potential too. So we will try our best from scout men to Brooke (Van Sickle) to EJ (Laure), I have full trust that everybody is going to do their best."
 Led by Fil-Am spiker Brooke Van Sickle, Nxled is coming off a 27-25, 25-22, 26-24 win against the Akari Chargers last Thursday.
 Advertisement 
 Cause of concern for the Chameleons was losing Jonah Sabete, who went down with an apparent left knee injury in the third set and was stretchered off the court.
 The athletic wing spiker looks like she avoided a serious injury, though.
 "So, the tests and the PT's I've done with Jonah, they look all negative. So we have a big hope that it's nothing serious. So this is why we are smiling a little more," said Guidetti.
 Meanwhile, Jema Galanza said that Creamline has to reset, as it always does, and take on Nxled.
 Advertisement 
 "We'll just have to fight again against Nxled," said Galanza, who led the Cool Smashers against the Flying Titans with 16 points, 13 excellent receptions, and 11 digs.
 In the first game, the already-eliminated teams Akari Chargers and the Zus Coffee Thunderbelles battle at 1 p.m.
